messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [REDACTED]

Age: 34 years

Sex: Female

Medical Record Number: [REDACTED]

Admission Date: [REDACTED]

Discharge Date: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to the emergency unit with complaints of moderate lower abdominal pain predominantly on the right side for the past 3 weeks. She did not present with any other symptoms such as fever, inappetence, nausea, or vomiting. A total abdomen ultrasonography (USG) was conducted, which revealed that the patient was in the second trimester of pregnancy without any evident alterations related to the pregnant uterus, the placenta, or the fetus. However, the iliac fossa was directed and revealed that the caecal appendix was thicker in the body portion, reaching a maximal transverse diameter of 9.2mm, which is above normal levels. The MRI results also corroborated the presence of lipomatosis in the appendix.

The patient was discharged after being prescribed analgesia, and she did not report any return of symptoms during follow-up.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Condition at Discharge:
 
At the time of discharge, the patient was stable, and her vital signs were normal.

Discharge Medications:

The patient was not prescribed any medication at the time of her discharge.

Follow-Up:

The patient was advised to continue her follow-up visits to her obstetrician and/or primary care physician.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible is lipomatosis of the appendix, a fatty thickening of the appendix shown on ultrasound and MRI as the cause of the right-sided abdominal pain. It is a non-inflammatory disease of the appendix in chapter K, category K38 (other diseases of appendix), with the pregnancy treated as incidental. If coded as complicating pregnancy under the Australian rule that a pregnancy is assumed affected unless documented as incidental, O99 would precede it.

CODE: K38
